introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. English Language 2 (0730), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2026. Paper 2: Section A - Composition; Section B - Prescribed Texts; Section C - Creative Writing. Duration: two hours fifteen minutes.**

Instructions to candidates: ANSWER ONE QUESTION FROM EACH SECTION. ALL QUESTIONS CARRY EQUAL MARKS.

Read all instructions on BOTH the question paper and the answer booklet very carefully. Failure to obey these instructions or to number your work as on the question paper will cause you to lose marks.

Any unusual mark, sign or unnecessary disclosure of your identity will be considered as an attempt to cheat and will earn you a penalty.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

A pre-prepared or memorised answer will earn you little or no marks.
enonce_intro_markdown:
**SECTION B - PRESCRIBED TEXTS (20 marks)**

Choose ONE question below and answer it.

**1. *Read the following extract and answer the questions below it.***

You are perfectly right, Your Eminence, but I must tell you the truth now. I have never seen the four walls of a secondary school in my life, talk less of the university. In primary school, I had an uncle who was the Chairman of that school where they train Administrators. My father helped choose a wife for him and in gratitude he had asked my father to give him any of his sons to help where he was working. My father chose me. But I was still in class four. After two years, he came back to say that that exam had been launched, and that it was his last year to be Chairman there. My father told him that I repeated, so I was still in Class Five. He told my father that he would register me, certificate or no certificate. In that examination that was meant for first degree holders, I found myself passing without having had the First School Leaving Certificate yet! My father celebrated! I didn't know what it was all about, but that's how I found myself here.

*(Extract printed in the paper without a title or an author; no line numbers are printed.)*

questions.enonce_markdown: **a).** Briefly recount what prompts the speaker to make this revelation. **(4 marks)**
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Model answer (4 marks)**

The speaker is prompted by what the person he calls "Your Eminence" has just said or assumed about him. The opening words, "You are perfectly right, Your Eminence, but I must tell you the truth now", show that he first agrees with the remark and then feels bound to correct the impression it gives: the speaker holds a position that a person would normally reach only after a long education, and he cannot let this false impression stand. (2 marks)

His conscience and honesty do the rest. He decides to confess that he has "never seen the four walls of a secondary school", and he then explains how an uncle's influence, his father's choice and an examination meant for degree holders brought him to his present position without the proper qualifications. (2 marks)

**Method.** "Briefly recount" asks for the cause (what triggers the speech) in your own words, in two or three sentences, not a copy of the whole extract. Notice the linking word "but": it shows that the speaker is answering someone and contradicting what that person believes.

questions.enonce_markdown: **b).** Identify two expressions that reveal the trait of honesty. **(4 marks)**
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Model answer (4 marks: 1 mark for each expression, 1 mark for each explanation)**

1. **"I must tell you the truth now."** The word "must" shows that the speaker feels a moral duty to be truthful, even though the truth will cost him his good reputation.
2. **"I have never seen the four walls of a secondary school in my life, talk less of the university."** He openly admits a fact that he could have hidden; the exaggeration ("never seen the four walls") stresses that his confession is complete and frank.

Other acceptable choices: "I didn't know what it was all about, but that's how I found myself here" (he does not pretend to understand or deserve what happened to him).

**Method.** Quote the exact words, then explain in one sentence why they show honesty.

questions.enonce_markdown: **c).** Pick out two abstract nouns and transform them to adverbs. **(2 marks)**
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Model answer (2 marks: 1 mark each)**

| Abstract noun in the extract | Adverb |
|---|---|
| **truth** | **truthfully** |
| **gratitude** | **gratefully** |

Other possible pairs: *eminence* becomes *eminently*; *certificate* is a concrete noun and *celebrated* is a verb, so they do not count.

**Method.** An abstract noun names a quality, feeling or idea that cannot be touched (truth, gratitude). Then form the adverb from the related adjective: *truth* gives *truthful*, which gives *truthfully*; *gratitude* gives *grateful*, which gives *gratefully*. Check that the adverb exists: *"truthly"* does not.

questions.enonce_markdown: **d).** Identify and list any four themes found in this extract. **(4 marks)**
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Model answer (4 marks: 1 mark per theme, with a short justification)**

1. **Education and certification:** the speaker has a high position without the schooling that normally leads to it; the extract questions the value of certificates ("certificate or no certificate").
2. **Corruption and nepotism (patronage):** an uncle who is Chairman uses his position to register a boy who lacks the qualifications, in return for a family favour ("in gratitude").
3. **Honesty and confession:** the speaker chooses to tell "the truth" about his past.
4. **Family loyalty and paternal ambition:** the father gives his son in return for the favour of a wife and celebrates the success ("My father celebrated!").

Other acceptable themes: the abuse of power, chance and the irony of success, social mobility.

**Method.** A theme is an idea that the writer develops, written as a noun phrase (not a sentence). Give four DIFFERENT ideas; two answers that say the same thing earn one mark only.

questions.enonce_markdown: **e).** Use any other two prescribed texts to discuss characters who portray honesty as a character trait. **(6 marks)**
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Corrige de methode (the other prescribed texts are not available for this model answer)**

The question asks you to discuss honest characters in TWO prescribed texts other than the extract. Use this plan (about 3 marks for each text):

1. **Link** (one sentence): honesty is shown in the extract by a speaker who confesses an uncomfortable truth.
2. **First text**: name the text and its writer; name ONE character who is honest; give one precise episode in which he or she tells the truth, refuses to lie or refuses a dishonest advantage; say what it costs or gains the character; say what the writer wants the reader to feel (admiration, respect, criticism of the dishonest society around).
3. **Second text**: the same four steps, preferably with a different kind of honesty (honesty in speech, in work, in public service, with oneself).
4. **Conclusion** (one or two lines): what the two characters have in common with the speaker of the extract.

**Marking.** The marks go to the choice of two OTHER texts, accurate and specific examples, and an explanation of how honesty is portrayed. A retelling of the plot, or a text from which no honest character can be named, earns little.
